# Sync contacts across systems: HubSpot & Notion

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers backups work end to end across HubSpot, Notion, Slack and Twilio.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Load Previous Snapshot
3. Fetch Changes Since Watermark
4. Normalize Records
5. Fingerprint for Idempotency
6. Drop Already-Processed Items
7. Upsert into HubSpot
8. Advance Watermark
9. Persist Watermark (Notion)
10. Row Counts Match?
11. Raise Drift Alarm
12. Enrich with Reference Data
13. Fold In Enrichment Fields
14. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
15. Archive Row Snapshot
16. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
17. Record Sub-workflow Result
18. Load Previous Snapshot 2
19. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
20. Stamp Completion Time
21. Persist Run Metadata
22. Cap Batch Volume
23. Align Field Names
24. Stamp Processing Time
25. Tag Pipeline Metadata
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
28. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing backups work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Load Previous Snapshot → Fetch Changes Since Watermark → Normalize Records → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Upsert into HubSpot → Advance Watermark → Persist Watermark (Notion) → Row Counts Match? → Raise Drift Alarm → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Load Previous Snapshot 2 → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Align Field Names → Stamp Processing Time → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and Notion aligned by hand for backups
- Backups work where "Fetch Changes Since Watermark" is still a manual step before HubSpot
- Backups work that only reaches HubSpot on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and Notion in step for backups, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in HubSpot or Notion are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this backups build
- A failed HubSpot or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this backups build
- Every backups run leaves an audit row behind, alongside HubSpot
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for backups

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; HubSpot private-app token; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2; Twilio SID + token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The pipeline is incremental, not full-refresh: it stores a watermark (the last-seen timestamp) and only asks the source for records newer than that, which is what keeps a scheduled re-run cheap instead of re-pulling the entire dataset every time. The tradeoff is that a failed watermark write must be safe to retry — which is exactly why the destination write is an upsert, not a plain insert.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Manually roll the watermark back and re-run — confirm the upsert makes the replay safe (no duplicates).
2. Trigger a reconcile mismatch on purpose and confirm the drift alarm fires.
3. Point the source at a different platform and see how little else in the workflow has to change.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Twilio SID + token**
Twilio Console → Account Info → Account SID + Auth Token.
_Gotcha:_ The `from` number must be one you own in Twilio. Trial accounts only send to verified numbers.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your backups process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Twilio: an API key/secret pair scoped to messaging, not the account SID and auth token.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole backups payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
